title: Membership cards + API key quota UX grooming
content:
Quick notes from grooming session (1/10/2025) — purpose: converge on a compact, scannable team/org settings UI that surfaces membership, RBAC preview, API key state and quota, and fast audit filters. This doc merges wireframe ideas + acceptance criteria + backlog tickets.

Summary / problem statement:
- Admins need to quickly understand who has access, what level it is, and whether API keys/service accounts are healthy. Current console has separate pages for members, keys, and audit logs — switching context is slow.
- We want a compact "membership card" pattern on the team view that reduces clicks and highlights risky items (expired keys, wildcard scopes, missing 2FA). Also show per-key quota usage and rotation state inline.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-action for common workflows: revoke key, rotate service account, change role, view recent audit entries. Target median task time < 30s for revoke/rotate.
- Make risk signals visible at glance (expired keys, keys without last-used timestamp, org-level roles).
- Keep layout compact for teams of 10–100 without heavy vertical scroll.

Personas:
- Platform admin (SRE/platform): cares about quotas, usage spikes, quick revoke/rotate
- Product manager/engineer: needs to check which service accounts are used by a route and whether quota impacts feature tests
- Security reviewer: wants audit links and evidence of rotation, 2FA and key scope constraints

Wireframe notes (visualize cards, hover/flyout interactions):
1) Team membership row -> membership card (compact)
   - Left: avatar or initials, member name, primary email (muted).
   - Middle: role chip(s) (primary role visible; secondary roles shown as +n). Clicking role chip opens a small flyout with: role description, permissions preview (top 5 perms), "what changes if I downgrade" quick diff.
   - Right: action menu (more_vert) with quick actions: change role, send invite/resend, remove. Long press to multi-select for bulk ops.
   - Visual risk ribbon (thin left border) that changes color: green (ok), amber (stale 2FA/last login >90d), red (dangerous org-level role or externally shared). Tooltip explains why.

2) API Key / Service account embedded card (can appear as inline rows under member or as separate compact section)
   - Title line: key name + small badge (service-account / api-key) + created date
   - Status badges: active / expired / rotating / revoked (colored).
   - Quota usage bar: 0–100% with small numeric: "usage: 23% of monthly quota (12k/50k tokens)". Clicking opens mini-modal with per-route consumption breakdown and top consumers (routes/app ids).
   - Last used: relative timestamp (e.g., last used 3d ago) + small eye icon to open last 10 audit events for that key.
   - Inline actions: rotate (one-click triggers rotate flow with confirm), revoke, copy key (obscured with reveal), attach policy (opens policy dropdown).
   - Rotation state flow: if key is rotating, show progress with stepper: request made -> new key issued (staged) -> confirm cutover -> old key revoked. Include cancel button during staging.

3) Audit quick filter row (persisted at top of team view)
   - Quick chips: last 7d, key-activity, role-changes, failed-logins, system-events. Selecting a chip filters the embedded audit list (lazy-loaded).
   - Search box: free-text + Jira-like operators (user:, key:, route:). Searching for key:abc pre-filters embedded key list.
   - Export button (CSV) and small badge with most recent event timestamp.

Edge cases and rules:
- Very large teams (>500): switch to virtualized list but keep same card height. Hide avatars by default (toggle).
- Keys with wildcard scopes: show explicit warning badge and require 2-step confirmation for revoke/rotate.
- Orphaned keys (no owner): appear at bottom under "unowned keys" with suggested owner list and button to claim.
- Cross-org roles: highlight with purple ribbon and disallow local downgrade without org-admin approval.

Accessibility / mobile considerations:
- Cards must be keyboard navigable: role chip tabbable, flyout dismissible with Esc.
- Color contrast for ribbons meets AA. Use iconography + text for risk states (not color-only).
- On narrower screens: collapse middle content to role chip + kebab; expand full details on tap.

Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- AC1: Membership card displays name, primary role, last login, and risk ribbon for 95% of members in staging org.
- AC2: API key card shows quota bar and last-used; clicking "rotate" creates a staged key and presents a copyable value that expires after 10 minutes.
- AC3: Audit quick chips filter results within <500ms for cached queries; falls back to server-side with progress indicator for larger windows.
- AC4: Keyboard-only users can open role flyout, change role, and confirm change without a mouse.

Backlog tasks (rough):
- CON-842: membership-card component + risk ribbon (5d frontend)
- CON-910: inline key quota bar + usage modal (4d frontend + 2d backend metrics endpoint)
- CON-914: rotation wizard (6d frontend + 3d backend endpoints + PRD for safety)
- CON-921: audit quick chips + search operators (3d frontend + 2d backend)
- UX tasks: microcopy for danger confirmations, accessibility audit (2d)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What level of quota granularity do we show in the mini-modal? (per-route last 30 days vs per-day breakdown). Recommendation: default last 30 days with "details" option.
- Do we allow API key copy to be captured by browser clipboard events (privacy)? We should warn and log copy events to audit.
- Should staged keys auto-expire after 24h if not promoted? Proposal: 24h staged TTL, configurable by org policy.

Design artifacts and next steps:
- Low-fi sketch done in FigJam (link on CON-842 ticket).
- Next: sync with infra/metrics to confirm we can compute per-key route breakdown in 24h. Owner: Marco.
- Schedule usability session with 3 platform admins and 2 security reviewers (target week of 1/20).

Notes to engineers:
- Try to reuse existing member list virtualization and permissions API (members:list) to avoid duplicate reads.
- Backend should provide a lightweight "key-summary" endpoint that returns: id, name, type, status, last_used, monthly_quota, monthly_usage, owner_id, staged (bool), staged_expires_at. Keep payload small for list use.

Quirky ideas (parking lot):
- "Who broke this?" quick revert: show last role change and allow rollback for 5 minutes after change. Might be good for reducing mistakes for new admins.
- Heatmap overlay that shows peak token usage by route across last 24h for org-level keys (visual exploration for SRE).

If you are reviewing: focus feedback on the rotate UX and staged key TTL. If ok, I'll turn wireframes into figma frames and draft CON-842 PRD stub.

-- Lena H. (notes from grooming)
